question: I changed my mind about a lamp that arrived three weeks ago. Can I still send it back?
query: return policy window for returns after delivery, eligibility of purchased items for return or refund after 21 days, change of mind returns, lamp (household lighting product)
answer: Yes, three weeks is within the 40-day return window, which is counted from the carrier's recorded delivery date [2][4]. The lamp must be unused (switching it on to test it is fine), in its original packaging with all accessories, and bought directly from Lantern Supply Co. [3]. It can't be a fuel lantern or oil lamp that has had fuel in it, or a final-sale item such as "Last Light" clearance or custom-engraved items [2].

## Relationship to the returns policy

The returns policy covers a change of mind within 40 days of delivery for an unused item. The
warranty covers a defect at any time within the warranty period, used or not. A fueled lantern
cannot be returned but can always be claimed under warranty. Agents should route a customer with
a working product who does not want it to the returns policy, and a customer with a product that
does not work to this document.

[2] customer-service-playbook.md > Returns
## Returns

The return window is 40 days from the delivery date recorded by the carrier. It is not counted
from the order date and, since Hearth 4.1 on May 19, 2026, not from the ship date. Check the
delivery scan in the Hearth admin before you tell a customer whether they are inside the window.
Orders delivered between November 1 and December 24 may be returned until January 31.

Returned items must be unused, in the original packaging, with all accessories. Any fuel lantern
or oil lamp that has had fuel in it cannot be returned; those go to warranty if there is a defect.
Clearance items marked "Last Light", custom-engraved items, gift cards, opened fuel, mantles,
wicks and other consumables are final sale.

[3] returns-policy.md > What can be returned
## What can be returned

An item is eligible for return when all of the following are true:

- It is unused. A lantern that has been switched on to check that it works is still unused. A
  lantern that has been taken on a trip is not.
- It is in its original packaging with all accessories, inserts, manuals and the warranty card.
- It was purchased from Lantern Supply Co. directly: the online store, by phone, or at the
  Frederick or Annapolis showroom. Items bought from another retailer go back to that retailer.
- It is not on the final-sale list below.

[4] release-notes.md > Highlights
### Highlights

Start a return online. A customer can begin a return from the order page, choose the items and
the reason, and get a return authorization number (RA-, six digits) at once instead of calling.
The prepaid return label at $8.50 is offered as an option and the amount is shown as a deduction
from the refund before the customer confirms.

The return window is now counted from the delivery date instead of the ship date. The window is
still 40 days, but the clock starts when the carrier records delivery, not when the box leaves
Hagerstown. This came out of the winter returns review: a box that sat with the carrier for
nine days was costing the customer nine days of their window. Orders shipped before May 19 had
their windows recalculated from the delivery date too.

Order lookup without an account. The order number and the email address on the order are enough
to see the status, tracking and the return option.

[5] customer-service-playbook.md > RET-01 Return window passed
### RET-01 Return window passed

Hello {name}, thank you for getting in touch about order {order}. Our return window is 40 days
from the delivery date, and tracking shows this order was delivered on {delivered}, which puts it
outside the window as of {deadline}. I am sorry I cannot open a return for it. If the item has a
defect, the standard warranty covers it for 2 years from purchase, and I would be glad to start a
warranty claim for you.
